news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

news.originalContent: Senior government officials admit that Israel's public opinion in the international community "has never been worse." According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten.  Follow Ynetnews on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | TikTok >> More stories: IDF releases name of fallen soldier in West Bank terror attack UN chief in Rafah crossing says world 'seen enough' of Gaza war Two Air Force pilots reminisce about their murdered brothers: 'There's no room for pain in the air' The officials added that the intensity of accusations made against Israel only increases, and attempts to equate Hamas's actions in Israel are being made, with allegations accusing IDF soldiers of sexually harassing Palestinian prisoners. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalTitle: 'We are in Shock': British Jews react to fatal terror attack - and fume at the 'lax response' of the UK
news.title: 'We are in Shock': British Jews react to fatal terror attack - and fume at the 'lax response' of the UK
news.originalSummary: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities. news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

French protests over the education and the cost of living have turned into widespread looting of major luxury stores — with rioters hitting Louis Vuitton, Hermes, and Apple.

Some designer brands, such as Dior, have reportedly hired private security teams to protect their stores in Paris after French police appeared to lose control of the streets of the capital.

More than 1,800 people have been arrested and President Emmanuel Macron addressed the nation, vowing to track down the looters who are trying to “bring down the Republic.”

Mobs looted the Galeries Lafayette — a luxury department store in Paris akin to Bergdorf Goodman or Harrods — with gangs of masked thugs seen smashing storefronts and raiding shelves on Saturday.

A picture showing a robust private security crew hired to protect a flagship Dior store in Paris went viral online.

In Marseille, looters targeted luxury brand Hermes, as well as stores selling jewelry, makeup and clothes.

Fire crews in the city said they had to put out a blaze that began in a designer shoe store.

In Bordeaux, a masked crowd was seen breaking down the doors to a Louis Vuitton store, as a parade of protesters waved red flags with hammer and sickle signs along the street.

In Lille, an Apple store was vandalized and looted, while in Nice, sportswear outlets and a motorcycle dealership were stormed.

Unrest broke out in France several weeks ago ostensibly as a student protest, but quickly devolved into an orgy of looting and riots.

Many other groups, including leftists and pro-Palestinian fanatics, have also used the riots as an excuse to force their agendas.

Dior had no faith in the French police to protect their store so they brought in their own security team to protect the flagship store in Paris tonight pic.twitter.com/aShDIzBeHS

Some 1,800 people were arrested on Saturday nationwide, while more than 500 cops were injured.

Rioters have also targeted France’s cultural heritage, with thugs torching the 140-year-old city hall in the southern city of Limoges, while Lyon’s tourist office was also set on fire.

Addressing the nation on Sunday, French President Macron said that “nothing justifies” the violence his country has seen this weekend.

“Tonight, we all feel anger and shame,” Macron said in the televised address, drawing a distinction between protesters with “legitimate demands” and “those who destroyed, smashed and looted.”

He said the looters “will have to pay back for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable.”

Macron blamed the “unrestrained violence” on “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”

It comes after Vice President J.D. Vance blamed mass immigration for the violent scenes in France.

“Western liberals imported the Third World into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” he wrote on X.

“I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” Vance added.

Former NFL player and TV personality Damien Woody shared a surprising health update with fans in an Instagram post on Sunday.

The former Jets offensive lineman, who left ESPN two months ago, revealed that he has been hospitalized after having his appendix and part of his colon removed following a colonoscopy.

“Want to give folks a health update,” Woody wrote. “Had a colonoscopy and from that have been hospitalized after having had my appendix and part of my colon removed. I want to thank all the doctors and nurses at Morristown Medical Center for the tremendous care I received. For the masses…mmm please get your checkups! Life is too short and too precious.”

The former Jets offensive lineman left ESPN two months ago after the network didn’t renew his contract in August. This ended his 15-year tenure as an NFL analyst.

Woody, a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Patriots, did not have his ESPN contract renewed after it expired in August, ending his 15-year tenure with the network.

Woody is now part of “The OG Football Show” on YouTube with fellow former ESPNers Trey Wingo, Mark Schlereth and Merril Hoge.

Woody announced his retirement from the NFL on July 26, 2011. Less than two weeks later, he made his ESPN debut. Over the years, Woody grew as an on-air personality and became a key contributor on “SportsCenter,” “NFL Live,” “Get Up,” “First Take” and other ESPN programs.

“Being a guy who had a serious speech impediment to working on tv was truly one of my proudest accomplishments. Looking forward to what God has in store for me next!” Woody said about his departure.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Lefty incumbent state Attorney General  Letitia James’ lead over GOPer Saritha Komatireddy has shrunk to just 6 points after the underdog’s strong debate performance, a bombshell Republican internal poll shows.

James now leads Komatireddy by just 50.7% to 44.7% — half of the Democratic AG’s 13-point spread in a Siena University survey last month, according to the new poll conducted for the GOP candidate and obtained by The Post.

About 4% of voters remain undecided, the latest survey found.

An analysis of the findings suggested that the Republican well-regarded former federal prosecutor’s Oct. 8 debate performance is largely responsible for shrinking the gap and provided her with momentum for her uphill battle in deep-blue New York during the home stretch.

“Letitia James sits at 50.7% with her negatives rising; Saritha Komatireddy is at 44.7% with a +15 net image,’’ wrote the GOP campaign’s pollster, OnMessage Inc., said in an Oct. 15 memo.

“The final three weeks are about one thing: putting Saritha in front of the voters who have not seen her yet, because the  ones who saw her debate are breaking to her by four to one.’’

One in five likely voters  surveyed said they watched the  debate.

Among those who watched, Komatireddy scores with them 81% to 19%. the poll showed.

Among the voters who did not watch the debate, James bested her foe 59% to 36%.

“That gap is the whole campaign in one number: the undecided and soft voters who see Saritha make the case against James move to her, and the ones who have not seen it stay with the incumbent simply by default,” OnMessage said.

OnMessage  surveyed 1,000 New York likely voters from October 12–14, with the poll having  a  margin of error of 2.8 percentage points.

Registered independent voters have shifted to Komatireddy, the survey added..In May, James was +3 with independents — 40% favorable, 37% unfavorable with the rest on the fence.

Now, James is 11 percentage points underwater with non-party-affiliated voters — 40% favorable to 51% unfavorable, with many  saying “very unfavorable.”

Komatireddy now leads James among independents 49% to 43%.

”This is where a well-funded closing message makes the difference,” the GOP pollster said.

Komatireddy is winning areas where Republicans need to perform well.

She leads James on Long Island 57% to 41% and the broader downstate suburbs 54% to 44% and upstate 50% to 44%.

James is ahead because of her huge margin in New York City, where she bests Komatireddy 65% to 30%.

Komatireddy leads among men 53% to 43%,  non-college voters 50% to 45%, and in terms of voters ages 46 to 55, 51% to 46%, according to the survey. The memo did not specify James’s lead among women.

The analysis noted that James only defeated underfunded Republican challenger Michael Henry by 9 percentage points when she won her second term in 2022.

But Komatireddy will have to peel away some soft or persuadable James backers to pull off an upset, the pollster noted.

Polling analyst Nate Silver gave OnMessage an A rating as one of the most accurate pollsters during the 2024 election cycle.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

As a federal prosecutor in Brooklyn’s Eastern District of New York, Komatireddy handled some of its most high-profile cases involving international terrorism, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, and public corruption.

James has meanwhile filed numerous lawsuits to block controversial actions taken by the Trump administration, including for allegedly providing energy companies $1.4 billion in funds to cancel four critical offshore wind projects, and on other funding and policy issues.

James has garnered nationwide attention for prosecuting Trump and his namesake company for fraudulent practices.

“Saritha Komatireddy wouldn’t protect New Yorkers from fraudsters or the federal government, because they’re the ones propping up her candidacy,’’ a James campaign spokeswoman told The Post on Sunday when asked about the new poll.

“Trump endorsed her, and she’d repay him by looking the other way while he sows chaos in New York.”

James  also commissioned a sexual misconduct probe of ex-Gov. Andrew Cuomo that triggered the Democrat’s resignation from office in 2021, even as he denied wrongdoing.

“There has been a tremendous surge of interest in Saritha and her vision for New York since her overwhelming debate victory over Ms. James,’’ said Saritha for New York campaign manager Isabelle Daigle to The Post.

“We’re seeing Democrats and independents joining with Republicans all across the state because of Saritha’s no-nonsense, apolitical approach to crime, homelessness, and fraud.

“Our polling data is internal, but we’re happy to report that we have extraordinary momentum on our side going into the final two weeks of this election. We like where we are, while understanding that we will have to work twice as hard to earn the individual votes of New Yorkers of all backgrounds over the next 15 days.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent knocked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for publicly accusing the Trump administration of throttling his country’s access to a military version of Starlink, which is critical for battlefield communications.

Zelensky alleged that someone in the administration gave orders to slow down satellite internet in objects cruising at 160 km/h or more, which undermined Kyiv’s drone operations.

“President Trump and Secretary Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that,” Bessent told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday. “And I think it is very reckless for President Zelensky to make such a charge.”

“I don’t know anything about that, but we’ve been very clear. And, you know, President Zelensky should be very careful about making statements like this that aren’t true.”

The mystery surrounding the limiting of Ukraine’s Starshield access has been dominated by confusion and finger-pointing.

Initially, top Ukrainian and European officials blamed near-trillionaire tech guru Elon Musk for curbing “Starlink” access. But Musk later claimed it was the military version of Starlink known as Starshield that was throttled and indicated it came from the Trump administration. Musk and a top Ukrainian official also suggested it was being restored.

However, Zelensky said in a prerecorded interview that aired on NBC’s “Meet the Press” Sunday that the limit was still in effect.

“We [still] have [a] limitation. The speed is [a] maximum [of] 161 kilometers. Not miles, kilometers,” he said.

The slowing down of Starshield access came as President Trump was pressuring Ukraine to back down on its drone strikes on Russian energy targets.

Both Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the administration ordered the throttling, though a report from Reuters claimed that someone in the administration ordered it.

“Of course, the message came from government. I don’t know from whom, what cabinet, and et cetera. And I think it doesn’t work either way,” Zelensky said. “But it’s not my opinion. It’s [the] opinion of our generals, of our government.”

Around the time that the throttling was revealed, Zelensky claimed that the US stopped sharing critical intelligence with Ukraine about incoming ballistic missile attacks from Russia, something he said has since been reversed.

Bessent also defended Trump’s decision to ease up on sanctions regarding Russian diesel and postpone implementation of Russian sanctions included in a bi-partisan bill named after the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.

“The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo. And, you know, I will point out the UK in May waived their embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude,” Bessent said.

“Where’s the outrage for the rest of the world? President Zelensky does not criticize his European partners,” he added. “The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports $4 billion of Russian products. One-point-eight billion of that [is] fertilizer. Europeans import more than ten times that.”

Zelensky had talks with US special peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Sunday amid the souring relations and posted that peace would only come through “cooperation built on trust.”

Had a conversation with the American President’s envoys, Steve Witkoff @SEPeaceMissions and Jared Kushner @jaredkushner. Peace comes only through strength and cooperation built on trust. We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America’s… pic.twitter.com/eNFwsJkNJS

Trump’s diesel deal with Russian strongman Vladimir Putin came as he grapples with midterm headaches due to high prices of the fuel that is heavily used by farmers.

The Treasury secretary also stressed that the Trump administration has enacted aggressive sanctions against Russia since the president took office in January of last year.

“First of all, the sanctions were doubled. The Biden administration, in an act of incredible bravery,” Bessent said sarcastically, “doubled the sanctions on the way out, in January of 2025. But we did not take those down.”

“President Trump sanctioned the two largest Russian energy companies, Rosneft and Lukoil, which dealt a catastrophic blow to the Russian energy industry,” he went on. “So no one has been tougher on Russian sanctions than President Trump.”

#49ers OT Trent Williams, asked if he’ll have any mixed feelings playing Washington after spending the first 9 years of his career w/ them:“Sometimes I forget that I even played there. … I’ve (spent almost) as much time here as I did there.” pic.twitter.com/aZaj36AuXm

“Sometimes I forget that I even played there. I only played nine seasons there,” Williams told Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle on Saturday. “It’s been almost as much time here as I have there.”

Williams’ career began with the Commanders after he was selected by the team with the No.4 overall pick of the 2010 NFL Draft.

From 2012-2018, Williams was selected to seven consecutive Pro Bowls and helped Washington reach the playoffs in 2012 and 2015.

During the 2019 season, Williams was placed on Washington’s non-football injury list and missed the entirety of the year.

In 2020, he was granted permission to seek a trade and would end up being traded to the 49ers in exchange for a fifth-round pick of the 2020 NFL Draft and a third-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.

While Williams has appeared to have forgotten about his time in Washington, the team hasn’t.

In 2022, Williams was inducted into the team’s “90 greatest” players and coaches list as part of the team’s 90th anniversary.

Since Williams landed with San Francisco, he’s had a rejuvenated his career and has been a three-time consecutive first-team All-Pro from 2021-2023.

He’s also remained a constant at the left tackle position, as he’s appeared in 75 games for the 49ers, including last season where he started in 16 games.

Despite being 38 years old, Williams has been playing at a high level this season alongside the rest of the San Francisco offensive line as quarterback Brock Purdy has been sacked only three times this season. All three of which came last week.

The 49ers enter their Week 6 game against the Commanders with a 5-0 record and are coming off a thrilling 32-29 victory against the Seahawks last week.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Klint Kubiak said changes could be coming as the Raiders searched for answers to their struggling running game.

On Sunday, he followed through.

The Raiders coach benched Jackson Powers-Johnson in favor of Caleb Rogers at right guard to start Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills, turning his talk of potential adjustments into a tangible change along the offensive line.

It”s not known if it’s a full-game benching.

Whether the move produces the desired results remains to be seen. But Kubiak made clear that maintaining the status quo was no longer the only option.

For Powers-Johnson, the decision represents a setback and a challenge to work his way back into the lineup. For Rogers, it presents an opportunity to help address a problem that has made life considerably more difficult for the Raiders’ offense.

The running game is supposed to provide the foundation for Kubiak’s system, creating manageable down-and-distance situations and helping set up opportunities through the air. When it stalls, the effects extend well beyond the rushing totals.

Longer third downs. Fewer favorable situations for the quarterback. More chances for opposing defenses to dictate how possessions unfold.

Changing one player does not guarantee those problems disappear. Nor does benching Powers-Johnson mean the responsibility falls entirely on his shoulders. Effective run blocking requires coordination across the front, with execution and timing extending to everyone involved in the play.

But the switch underscores Kubiak’s willingness to try a different combination rather than simply wait for improvement.

Against Buffalo, the Raiders needed an offense capable of sustaining possessions and giving itself a chance to keep pace. Finding traction on the ground would help accomplish both.

Rogers now gets his chance to contribute to that effort.

The larger question is whether a different face at right guard can help produce a different result for the running game.

Kubiak had promised to consider changes. Sunday brought evidence that he meant it.

news.originalContent:

Tennessee earned its first win of the season in Indianapolis and did so without cornerback Alontae Taylor.

The offseason addition was on the sideline for Sunday’s 26-20 win over the Colts (2-4) due to a coach’s decision and not an injury.

Taylor has been critical for the Titans’ defense, playing 99.7% of defensive snaps in the Titans’ first five games of the season. He signed a three-year, $58 million contract ($42 million guaranteed) in March and has 19 tackles and one sack on the year.

The Titans (1-5) focused on upgradingtheirs secondary by adding Taylor and signing free agent cornerback Cor’Dale Flott to a three-year, $45 million deal.

Veteran free agent addition Josh Williams, who signed a two-year, $8 million contract in March, started in Taylor’s place, returning from injured reserve Saturday. Cornerback Isaiah Oliver was given the game-day elevation from the practice squad.

Tennessee’s secondary hasn’t been productive under new head coach Robert Saleh. The Titans so far only have three interceptions this season. Despite the low takeaways, Tennessee ranked 14th in passing yards allowed per game in the NFL (217.8) coming into the game.

The Titans were also without starting safety Kevin Winston Jr. due to a quad injury against the Colts.

Tennessee may be evenly matched against a Colts squad that has been bombarded with injuries at wide receiver.

The Colts will still be without recently extended Alec Pierce, who’s on the injury reserve with a left heel injury, and second-year tight end Tyler Warren is inactive with a groin injury.

The Titans earned their first division win since November 2024 with a victory on Sunday.

news.originalContent:

At this point, somebody might want to check whether the Los Angeles Rams’ special teams unit was built on an ancient burial ground.

Because whatever curse has been haunting the Rams’ kicking game apparently followed their newest kicker straight onto the field Sunday afternoon.

Blake Grupe, making his Rams debut after replacing Harrison Mevis earlier this week, drilled a 44-yard field goal to give Los Angeles an early 3-0 lead over the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium.

Seconds later, he was being helped off the field with a knee injury.

You can’t make this stuff up.

On the ensuing kickoff, Arizona returner Devin Duvernay broke through the Rams’ coverage unit, leaving Grupe as the last line of defense between him and the end zone.

The 5-foot-7, 150-pound kicker managed to force Duvernay out of bounds, saving a potential touchdown. Unfortunately, he injured his knee making the tackle and subsequently headed to the locker room with trainers.

Rams New Kicker Blake Grupe Tried To Tackle Somebody On The Kickoff And Ended Up Injuring Himself.The Rams Just Signed This Guy After Cutting Harrison Mevis.Rough Start. 😬 pic.twitter.com/0BDZRD1hzh

The Rams listed him as doubtful to return.

For the second consecutive game, Los Angeles’ kickoff coverage was so poor that its kicker was forced to make a touchdown-saving tackle.

Last Monday against Buffalo, it was the 6-foot-1, 250-plus-pound Mevis, nicknamed the “Thiccer Kicker,” who pushed the Bills’ returner out of bounds on the opening kickoff.

Mevis subsequently missed two field goals, including a potential overtime game-winner, prompting the Rams to release him Tuesday and sign Grupe off the New York Jets’ practice squad.

Now, after one successful kick, his replacement might be sidelined too.

Rams punter Ethan Evans was spotted practicing field goals on the sideline and could be pressed into emergency duty. If he attempts one, Evans would become the franchise’s ninth different field goal kicker since 2020.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Was this wheelie the best spot?

A brand-spanking new peloton of Citi Bikes has been sitting unused in their Queens docks for weeks — angering locals who say they’re too expensive, crowd the sidewalks and gobble up precious parking spaces,

Several stations popped up across Forest Hills in the past month, but are seemingly always full and underutilized.

“There are too many. It’s ridiculous. It’s out of control, and as you can see, no one is using them,” fumed Joe Augello, 70, an insurance broker who has lived in the nabe for three decades.

Augello pointed out that many Forest Hills residents are car drivers, but at least one of the dock stations was planted in front of private homes.

“People can’t walk the streets because these things are in the way. I mean, if you have somebody that had to walk here with a wheelchair or a stroller, you have to navigate the stupid bicycles,” Augello said.

Forest Hills now has 44 Citi Bike stations across both major and residential streets, as part of the network expansion announced earlier this week by Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

The network increased by 11%, with 234 total stations popping up in seven neighborhoods in Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

Augello said he started noticing the increase in docking stations in the last month or so.

“Especially what’s really ridiculous is when they have these stations in front of a private residence,” he added.

Lyft has other plans to add “hundreds of docks” within the existing service area this fall, including in Midtown, Chelsea, Williamsburg, Greenpoint and Gowanus, City Hall said.

But the growing network comes amid complaints that riding the silver electric bikes has become too expensive.

“A five-minute trip shouldn’t be $8. That sucks,” David Ruiz, 23, of Corona, who has coughed up the $220 for an annual electric membership because it’s more cost-effective than purchasing as-needed rides.

Other Queens residents griped that the bikes were taking away precious street parking opportunities — especially considering Forest Hills is a car town.

A DOB spokesperson said the city takes a “thoughtful approach” to identifying locations.

“Citi Bike is popular because it’s a convenient way to get around, and even in neighborhoods where there may be some skepticism at first, we see high ridership from residents who ultimately embrace the service,” the spokesperson said.

The city did not offer specifics on how Forest Hills was chosen.

Locals are going to take some convincing.

“I think it’s too much,” said Sergey Davydov, 41. “They take a lot of parking space. Not a lot of people use them — you see, it’s mostly always full.”

Arthur Feigenbaum agreed, calling the docks “a bad idea.”

“I don’t like them!” the 73-year-old said.

When asked whether he supports Mamdani’s Citi Bike expansion, Feigenbaum quipped: “I don’t agree with most of what he says.”

If the Giants do not make the playoffs, they will rue the final 83 seconds of the first half and first 159 seconds of the second half Sunday as the point where a promising season slipped off the rails.

The defense allowed three scores in that decisive span and the special teams committed a turnover as a comfortable 10-point lead disappeared in a hurry.

By the time the Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy after allowing 34 straight points and McCarthy turned in a magic fourth quarter, it was too late to prevent a 34-27 loss to the spiraling Saints at MetLife Stadium.

With Cam Skattebo benched due to ball-security issues, the Giants didn’t have enough playmaking until McCarthy led the offense to 17 unanswered fourth-quarter points and forced the Saints to get one first down to close out the game in the final two minutes.

The Saints fueled their comeback and snapped their three-game losing streak by scoring 17 points and running 17 offensive plays in between true offensive snaps for the Giants.

Daniel Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal – a gutsy call by head coach Kellen Moore considering Carlson already had missed from 55 – with 1:23 to go in the first half and Charlie Jones fumbled the ensuing kickoff.

And then the Giants fell one play short of a goal-line stand, allowing a 2-yard touchdown pass to a wide-open Bryce Lance as decoy Chris Olave drew a double team with one second remaining.

Suddenly, it was 10-10 after a half in which the Giants – especially a defense playing tight coverage, blitzing and flying around – felt in complete control.

The Giants kneeled out the clock and kicked off to start the third quarter.

Tyler Shough, who finished ahead of Jaxson Dart in the Offensive Rookie of the Year vote last season, led the Saints on back-to-back third-quarter touchdown drives. Tyrone Tracy Jr.’s great individual effort allowed him to turn a delayed route into a checkdown catch into a 17-yard touchdown catch. Tracy caught the pass, broke to his right, ran through a diving shoestring tackle by Pete Werner and dove head-first across the pylon for a 7-0 lead.

Dominic Zvada added a 34-yard field goal before the collapse began.

Facing the third-worst rushing defense in the NFL, the Giants’ rushing attack consisted of one 20-yard gain on a reverse to Darnell Mooney and 17 yards on 14 carries by all other ball-carriers combined over the first three quarters.

Demoting the popular Skattebo sent a locker-room message but backfired on the field because the Giants didn’t have his fearless running to fall back on as the offset to their weekly lack of explosive runs.

Najee Harris (four carries for two yards), Devin Singletary (three for five) and Tyrone Tracy Jr. (three for eight) combined for nine yards as Skattebo didn’t touch the ball until the fourth quarter.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Job seekers looking to make a career move at the start of the year might want to rethink their strategy.

A study from career platform Enhancv reveals that January and February bring a brutal mix of fierce competition and sluggish hiring – despite misconceptions that January is peak application season.

Enhancv analyzed 25 years of federal hiring data alongside five years of resume activity, pairing the data with a survey of U.S. recruiters and hiring managers to confirm the trend.

Most job hunters flood the market in January and February – right when hiring hits rock bottom. Resume downloads in January run 11.6% above average, representing a 51% surge compared to December.

This is where the “apply in January” misconception comes from, as people juxtapose January’s data to December’s dormant season. In reality, hires peak much later in the year.

Job listings peak three times a year: April, July, and October. The best window for applicants spans from May through August, with June crowned as the best month to apply.

June hiring surges 16.3% above average while candidate competition drops 8%. While listings pop in April, a crush of applicants negates the benefit.

Meanwhile, December ranks as the slowest month for hiring, sitting 26.5% below average—making it better suited for polishing resumes than submitting them.

Overall job openings have trended downward since 2022 as employers trim budgets.

To filter out broad macroeconomic shifts, the study compared each month to surrounding months within the same year, separating seasonal swings from broader economic slowdowns.

Recruiters overwhelmingly named April (12.7%), May (13.6%), and June (12.1%) as prime hiring months. A secondary spike arrives ahead of the holidays, with 30.8% of recruiters citing a seasonal boost in the fall.

Patience is key for applicants. While job posts surge in April, offers follow a few weeks later – 36% of recruiters say it takes two to four weeks to go from posting to job offer.

That sets off a clear pattern: April’s posting boom fuels May and June hiring, while a July surge keeps the momentum high through August.

The odds shift wildly throughout the year. June, May, and October give job hunters the best shot, while February heavily favors employers with massive crowds of applicants, though they battle for few open seats.

June takes the crown as the ultimate month to apply. Hiring jumps 16.3% above average just as applicant competition cools by 8%, making it the undisputed heavy-hitter for job seekers.

AI doesn’t help the equation. In September, AI was responsible for nearly 4,000 job cuts according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas, which tracks monthly public job cut announcements.

AI has been cited in more than 120,000 job cut announcements, becoming the attributing factor for 21% of all layoffs in 2026.

A private jet aborted its takeoff after it ran off the end of a runway at Harry Reid International Airport Sunday morning.

The aircraft, a Dassault Falcon 50 with tail number N200SG, was departing from Runway 1L at about 11 a.m. when it skidded off the runway and made contact with the airport’s perimeter fence.

“At approximately 11 a.m., upon departure, a general aviation aircraft skid off runway 1L at LAS and made contact with the perimeter fence. There are no known injuries at this time,” the airport said.

“Runways 1R and 1L will be closed for inspection, and travelers may experience some delays. We will provide updates as more information becomes available,” authorities said.

A flight-tracking map shared on social media by Red Wave Press shows the jet moving slowly from its taxi position and turning onto the runway.

The plane then continues past the end of the pavement before veering to the right and coming to a complete stop. The airport said the aircraft made contact with the perimeter fence.

The Federal Aviation Administration has issued a ground stop for the airport, citing an “aircraft emergency.” Airport officials said the stop may result in delays and urged travelers to check with their airlines about flight status.

FAA registry records show that the aircraft, a three-engine business jet, is owned by Jacks Wings LLC of Boca Raton, Florida.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Astronomers have discovered the first white dwarf “zombie” star with a “ghostly green glow” that they say it got from eating the rocky debris of dead planets.

“It feels like something out of science fiction,” said astrophysicist Mark Hollands, whose team from the University of Warwick announced its findings last week.

The zombie WD J1330+6435 is in the Milky Way, although about 280 light-years from our solar system, and can be faintly seen in the constellation Draco, the scientists said.

The discovery marked the first time researchers have seen a “green” star — and discovered that the color of such super-dense “zombie” stars can be changed by elements it absorbs such as carbon, calcium, and sodium.

“Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like ‘perfect radiators,’ so their color is set almost entirely by temperature,” Hollands told Space.com, explaining that cool stars look orange and hot stars appear pale blue. “But nobody had really looked into what else might be possible for white dwarfs.

“It turns out these incredibly dense stars can produce colors nobody expected, and some of them genuinely surprised me.

“The traces of sodium in the atmosphere of this white dwarf absorb the orange part of the spectrum, leaving behind a ghostly green glow,” Hollands said.

“Imagine standing on a planet and looking up at a green star.”

White dwarfs in general are the leftover stellar core of a star that has stopped producing nuclear fuel and shed its outer layer during its red-giant phase.

Without fusion to sustain itself, it devours planets, asteroids and other heavenly bodies that get pulled into its supercharged gravity, leading it to be called a “zombie” star in the phase because it “lives” after “death.”

One of those celestial snacks — rocky material from a nearby planet containing calcium, lithium, and sodium — turned WD J1330+6435 green, scientists said.

Dwarf stars that have consumed high levels of carbon would be pink or purple, while those that consumed asteroids, comets or old planets would be more yellow. Cooling dying stars with a mixed hydrogen and helium atmosphere would appear cyan or pale blue, according to researchers.

In addition to spotting the green star, astronomers were also seeing red — announcing a white dwarf that could be the reddest star ever observed.

Stationed about 48 light-years away, WD J1011+2845 has a deep convection zone that brings carbon from its core to its surface — creating a salmon-pink glow, according to the study.

Scientists estimate that only about 3 percent of white dwarfs have vibrant coloring like the two they touted.

“One in thirty might not sound like a huge fraction, but across the entire population of white dwarfs in the universe, that is still a lot of oddly colored stars out there,” said Boris Gänsicke of the Department of Physics at Warwick to the outlet.

“Yet if we take the median across a representative population of white dwarfs, we found that the average white dwarf really is white.”

Earth’s sun will run out of hydrogen and engulf the inner planets of our solar system before entering its white dwarf phase in about 5 billion years.

news.originalContent:

The state Democratic Party has quietly approved a resolution condemning antisemitism as it battles back against the notion its leaders “are soft’’ on anti-Jewish hate.

The little-noticed measure was overwhelmingly passed earlier this month — moments after Jay Jacobs, who is Jewish and a supporter of Israel, was overwhelmingly re-elected as party chairman over insurgent candidate and Otsego County Democratic Party Chair Caitlin Ogden.

“I feel very good about it. I’m constantly responding to claims that Demcrats are soft on antisemitism,” Jacobs told The Post.

The New York Democratic Party, in its official press release put out Oct. 1 about the election of officers, made no mention of the proposed resolution.

Jacobs insisted that the omission was an oversight and got lost amid the focus on the party’s internal elections, including his own.

“That was a mistake. We dropped the ball,” he said.

“I want the people to know what the New York Democratic Party is doing to confront antisemitism. It’s consequential,” Jacobs said.

Leftists in the party had been pushing to oust Jacobs, who is also the Nassau County Democratic Party chairman, for alleged lackluster leadership and refusing to endorse radical New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani last year.

Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman, during his debate last week with Democratic incumbent Kathy Hochul, accused Hochul ally Mamdani of being an “antisemite.”

Jacobs’ more moderate leanings within the party — including his support of Israel — have rankled some progressives and Israel-bashers.

The new antisemitism-related resolution states: “Contemporary antisemitism often manifests through subtle rhetoric, coded language and dog whistles including, but not limited to, Holocaust denial and distortion; modern blood libels depicting Jewish people as inherently murderous or targeting children; conspiracy theories alleging Jewish control of governments, financial institutions, or the media; accusations of dual loyalty to Israel; and the use of Israel as a pretext for hostility toward Jewish people or Jewish institutions.

“Antiisemitism continues to be expressed through overt acts of intimidation and violence, including assaults on Jewish individuals, vandalism of Jewish institutions, the display of swastikas, Nazi symbols and Nazi salutes, threats against synagogues and schools, and other acts intended to intimidate or terrorize Jewish communities.

“No person should be subjected to violence, targeted discrimination, intimidation, or harassment because of their religion, heritage, or ethnicity; now, therefore, be it. Resolved, that the New York State Democratic Committee: Condemns all antisemitic violence, intimidation, discrimination, and aggression,” the measure states.

The resolution applauded Hochul’s approval of a buffer-zone law that particularly criminalizes harassment outside synagogues and other houses of worship.

The statement also lauded Mamdani’s 900% increase in funding for the Office of Hate Crime Prevention in this year’s city budget.

Jacobs defended Mamdani to The Post, saying his pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel views do not make him an antisemite.

“Zohran Mamdani is not an antisemite. He sympathizes with the Palestinian cause, and he opposes some of the actions of the Israeli government. I have disagreements with him on some of the issues,” he said.

“The fact that Bruce Blakeman said that is an effort to get votes, and it’s shameful.”

The Dem Party’s new resolution also calls for legislation and resources to combat antisemitism and hate crimes and educational initiatives statewide that teach the history, contributions and experiences of Jewish people, the Holocaust and current manifestations of antisemitism.

The statement calls on all individuals campaigning for or holding Democratic Party positions to abide by the spirit and intent of the hate fighting party platform.

Jacobs insisted that the omission was an oversight and got lost amid the focus on the party’s internal elections, including his own.

“That was a mistake. We dropped the ball,” he said.

“I want the people to know what the New York Democratic Party is doing to confront antisemitism. It’s consequential,” Jacobs said.

Leftists in the party had been pushing to oust Jacobs, who is also the Nassau County Democratic Party chairman, for alleged lackluster leadership and refusing to endorse radical New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani last year.

Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman, during his debate last week with Democratic incumbent Kathy Hochul, accused Hochul ally Mamdani of being an “antisemite.”

Jacobs’ more moderate leanings within the party — including his support of Israel — have rankled some progressives and Israel-bashers.

The new antisemitism-related resolution states: “Contemporary antisemitism often manifests through subtle rhetoric, coded language and dog whistles including, but not limited to, Holocaust denial and distortion; modern blood libels depicting Jewish people as inherently murderous or targeting children; conspiracy theories alleging Jewish control of governments, financial institutions, or the media; accusations of dual loyalty to Israel; and the use of Israel as a pretext for hostility toward Jewish people or Jewish institutions.

“Antiisemitism continues to be expressed through overt acts of intimidation and violence, including assaults on Jewish individuals, vandalism of Jewish institutions, the display of swastikas, Nazi symbols and Nazi salutes, threats against synagogues and schools, and other acts intended to intimidate or terrorize Jewish communities.

“No person should be subjected to violence, targeted discrimination, intimidation, or harassment because of their religion, heritage, or ethnicity; now, therefore, be it. Resolved, that the New York State Democratic Committee: Condemns all antisemitic violence, intimidation, discrimination, and aggression,” the measure states.

The resolution applauded Hochul’s approval of a buffer-zone law that particularly criminalizes harassment outside synagogues and other houses of worship.

The statement also lauded Mamdani’s 900% increase in funding for the Office of Hate Crime Prevention in this year’s city budget.

Jacobs defended Mamdani to The Post, saying his pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel views do not make him an antisemite.

“Zohran Mamdani is not an antisemite. He sympathizes with the Palestinian cause, and he opposes some of the actions of the Israeli government. I have disagreements with him on some of the issues,” he said.

“The fact that Bruce Blakeman said that is an effort to get votes, and it’s shameful.”

The Dem Party’s new resolution also calls for legislation and resources to combat antisemitism and hate crimes and educational initiatives statewide that teach the history, contributions and experiences of Jewish people, the Holocaust and current manifestations of antisemitism.

The statement calls on all individuals campaigning for or holding Democratic Party positions to abide by the spirit and intent of the hate fighting party platform.

news.originalContent:

WASHINGTON — President Trump rolled out new renovation plans for the iconic East Potomac Golf Course and announced that it will be shut down for the next 15 months for the revamp.

Renovations that would transform it into a “one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World” would begin Nov. 15, Trump claimed Sunday, as he glossed over the legal hurdles he has faced in the project.

“The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect,” Trump posted on Truth Social. “It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall.”

“When the East Potomac Course was originally built, it was famous for no trees, with views of Washington, D.C., for all to see, but now, it is completely overgrown, dysfunctional, and unsafe,” he added.

The Trump administration has faced legal snarls in its effort to renovate the golf course, with a judge temporarily stymying it from removing trees after more than 400 were cut down.

In May, District Judge Ana Reyes ordered the Trump administration to give notice of plans to cut down more than 10 trees.

On the Friday before Columbus Day weekend, just before the close of business, officials alerted the court of plans to cut “up to 529 trees.” By Saturday, some 430 trees were chopped down, resulting in Reyes scheduling an emergency hearing Monday.

The teed-off judge responded to Trump’s Sunday post and ordered the government to notify her by 8 p.m. whether a Friday court filing that stated the rebuilding plan was in the “preliminary” stages had changed.

The administration, which is being sued by the DC Preservation League and several other plaintiffs, is pushing for Reyes to be replaced.

Trump, who has publicly boasted about winning multiple tournaments at his own golf clubs, tapped Tom Fazio with the new designs.

Prior plans for the renovations at the course, which is about 2.3 miles away from the White House, miffed DC residents due to the apparent lack of biking and running paths there for the public. There have been numerous races at the 106-year-old park over the years.

For example, the Washington Area Bicyclist Association has championed a petition to protect Hains Point, a park and wildlife hub at the tip of East Potomac Park. The latest design Trump posted similarly appeared to get rid of those paths.

President Trump is a kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and hardworking man. I wish more Americans appreciated him. No one will ever make America great the way he has and continues to.It was an honor to work for him. pic.twitter.com/Tp4NizrhE2

A blurred-out map of the renovation plans was seen on Trump’s desk in a photo posted by his former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia.

The East Potomac Golf Links and the other two major DC courses had been overseen by the National Park Service and National Links Trust.

But in December of last year, the administration directed the NPS to end its 50-year lease with the National Links Trust.

“The United States Golf Association, PGA of America, and the PGA Tour have already been notified that they will soon have one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World to put on their list of great places to play, and hold Major Events,” Trump added.

Democracy Forward, the group representing the plaintiffs fighting Trump’s renovation plans, had said it intended to “protect this community jewel” from “unlawful and harmful intrusion.”

news.originalContent:
A fire broke out near Heruvit Forest on Saturday afternoon, and has yet to be contained, local media reported.

Firefighting teams were dispatched to the area to contain the fire, but are battling strong winds and complex terrain conditions.

Firefighting aircraft were carrying out airdrops in parallel with activities on the ground in an attempt to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading towards infrastructure and agriculture.

Individuals in the area have been evacuated. The public is asked not to go to the scene and to cooperate with emergency and rescue forces operating in the area.

This is a developing story.

news.originalTitle: France's Armed Forces Minister reaffirms no weapons being sold to Israel
news.title: France's Armed Forces Minister reaffirms no weapons being sold to Israel
news.originalSummary:
France's Armed Forces Minister, Sébastien Lecornu, reaffirmed that the country is not selling any weapons to Israel, he said on the France news channel LCI on Friday.

"And for good reason: Israel is one of the main competitors of French industries," he added.

news.originalTitle: «ما شما را تنها گذاشتیم»؛ روایت ژنرال‌های آمریکایی از زمستان سخت اوکراین
news.title: «ما شما را تنها گذاشتیم»؛ روایت ژنرال‌های آمریکایی از زمستان سخت اوکراین
news.originalSummary: اوکراین در آستانه زمستانی سخت با حملات روسیه به زیرساخت‌های انرژی و تردیدهایی درباره ادامه حمایت آمریکا روبه‌روست. در مجمع امنیتی ورشو، فرماندهان کنونی و پیشین ارتش آمریکا درباره آینده جنگ، سیاست‌های واشنگتن و نقش اروپا سخن گفتند. اما ارزیابی آن‌ها از شرایط اوکراین یکسان نبود.
